subject: maths
prompt_en: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 3 cm. What whole-number lengths can the third side be?
prompt_hi: Ek triangle ki do sides 7 cm aur 3 cm hain. Teesri side kaunsi poori-number lambaiyan ho sakti hai?
answer: 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9 cm: more than 7 − 3 = 4 and less than 7 + 3 = 10

subject: maths
prompt_en: A farmer wants a triangular fence. Two sides are 12 m and 20 m. His third side is 35 m. Can the fence close as a triangle? What lengths would work?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan triangle wali baad lagana chahta hai. Do sides 12 m aur 20 m hain. Teesri 35 m hai. Kya baad triangle ban ke band hogi? Kaunsi lambai chalegi?
answer: No: 12 + 20 = 32 is less than 35; the third side must be more than 8 m and less than 32 m

subject: maths
prompt_en: Describe what the compass arcs look like when you try to construct a triangle with 3 cm, 4 cm and 9 cm.
prompt_hi: 3 cm, 4 cm aur 9 cm ka triangle banane ki koshish mein compass ke arcs kaise dikhenge, batao.
answer: After drawing 9 cm, the 3 cm and 4 cm arcs from its ends stop short with a gap between them, so there is no third vertex

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to decide with one quick check whether three lengths can make a triangle.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki ek jaldi ke check se kaise pata karein ki 3 lambaiyon se triangle banega ya nahi.
answer: Find the longest; if it is less than the sum of the other two, yes; if it is equal or more, no

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: can 5 cm, 5 cm and 11 cm make a triangle?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: kya 5 cm, 5 cm aur 11 cm se triangle banega?
answer: No: 5 + 5 = 10, which is less than 11

subject: maths
prompt_en: How many altitudes does a triangle have?
prompt_hi: Ek triangle ke kitne altitude hote hain?
answer: 3, one from each vertex

subject: maths
prompt_en: In a right triangle, which sides are also altitudes?
prompt_hi: Right triangle mein kaunsi sides altitude bhi hoti hain?
answer: The two sides that make the right angle; each is the altitude to the other

subject: maths
prompt_en: Take a triangle with one wide angle, like 130°. Predict: when you drop an altitude from one of the other two vertices, will it land inside the triangle?
prompt_hi: Ek triangle lo jiska ek angle bahut bada ho, jaise 130°. Andaaza lagao: baaki do mein se kisi vertex se altitude giraoge toh kya woh triangle ke andar girega?
answer: No: it lands outside, on the extension of the opposite side

subject: maths
prompt_en: From vertex A, one line goes to the midpoint of BC and another meets BC at 90°. Which is the altitude? When could they be the same line?
prompt_hi: Vertex A se ek line BC ke midpoint tak jaati hai aur doosri BC se 90° par milti hai. Altitude kaunsi hai? Dono ek hi line kab ho sakti hain?
answer: The one meeting at 90° is the altitude; they are the same line when AB = AC (an isosceles triangle with apex A)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why do we sometimes have to extend a side to draw an altitude?
prompt_hi: Altitude banane ke liye kabhi-kabhi side ko aage kyun badhana padta hai?
answer: In an obtuse triangle the perpendicular from a vertex misses the opposite side itself; it meets the line of that side only after we extend it

subject: maths
prompt_en: Isha drew the altitude of a tilted triangle as a line straight down the page from the top vertex. It does not meet the opposite side at a right angle. What went wrong?
prompt_hi: Isha ne tirchhe triangle ka altitude top vertex se page ke seedha neeche tak banaya. Woh saamne wali side se right angle par nahi milta. Galti kya hui?
answer: An altitude must be perpendicular to the opposite side, not vertical on the page; she should draw it at 90° to that side

subject: maths
prompt_en: Om says, 'This obtuse triangle has only one altitude because the other two would go outside.' Is he right?
prompt_hi: Om kehta hai, 'Is obtuse triangle ka sirf ek altitude hai kyunki baaki do bahar jaayenge.' Kya woh sahi hai?
answer: No: every triangle has three altitudes; in an obtuse triangle two of them fall outside

subject: maths
prompt_en: The front of a tent is a triangle. A pole from the top goes straight down to the ground and meets it at 90°. Is the pole an altitude? What does its length tell you?
prompt_hi: Tent ka saamne wala hissa triangle hai. Upar se ek pole seedha zameen tak jaata hai aur 90° par milta hai. Kya pole altitude hai? Uski lambai kya batati hai?
answer: Yes: it is the altitude from the top vertex to the ground side, and its length is the height of the tent

subject: maths
prompt_en: A ladder leans against a wall, making a triangle with the ground. Which segment is the altitude from the top of the ladder to the ground, and how would you measure it?
prompt_hi: Ek seedhi deewar se lagi hai aur zameen ke saath triangle banati hai. Seedhi ke upar wale sire se zameen tak altitude kaunsa segment hai, aur use kaise naapoge?
answer: The part of the wall from the ladder's top straight down to the ground (perpendicular to the ground); measure it along the wall

subject: maths
prompt_en: Describe how to fold a paper triangle to make an altitude crease from one vertex.
prompt_hi: Batao ki kaagaz ke triangle ko kaise modein ki ek vertex se altitude ki crease bane.
answer: Fold so the opposite side lies on top of itself and the crease passes through the vertex; that crease is perpendicular to the side

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to draw all three altitudes of an obtuse triangle.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki obtuse triangle ke teeno altitude kaise banate hain.
answer: From each vertex draw a line at 90° to the opposite side; for the two sides next to the obtuse angle, extend them first; two altitudes fall outside

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: what is an altitude of a triangle?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: triangle ka altitude kya hota hai?
answer: A segment from a vertex that meets the opposite side (or its extension) at 90°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. Find the third.
prompt_hi: Triangle ke do angle 50° aur 60° hain. Teesra nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: A right triangle has one angle of 35°. Find the other two angles.
prompt_hi: Ek right triangle ka ek angle 35° hai. Baaki do angle nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. Classify it by sides.
prompt_hi: Ek triangle ki sides 5 cm, 5 cm aur 8 cm hain. Sides ke hisaab se iska naam batao.
answer: Isosceles (two equal sides)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict: if you tear off the three corners of any paper triangle and place them side by side, what shape will they make? Then try.
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: kisi bhi kaagaz ke triangle ke 3 kone phaad ke saath rakhoge toh kaunsi shape banegi? Phir try karo.
answer: A straight line, which is 180°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare a triangle with angles 90°, 45°, 45° and one with 60°, 60°, 60°. Name each by angles and by sides.
prompt_hi: 90°, 45°, 45° wale triangle ko 60°, 60°, 60° wale se compare karo. Dono ka naam angles aur sides ke hisaab se batao.
answer: First: right and isosceles; second: acute and equilateral

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why do the angles of every triangle add to 180°? Use a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side.
prompt_hi: Har triangle ke angles ka jod 180° kyun hota hai? Ek vertex se saamne ki side ke parallel line kheench ke samjhao.
answer: The parallel line makes alternate angles equal to the two base angles; together with the top angle they lie along a straight line, which is 180°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Aman says a triangle can have two angles of 100° if the third angle is 'very small'. Check his claim.
prompt_hi: Aman kehta hai ki agar teesra angle 'bahut chhota' ho toh triangle ke do angle 100° ho sakte hain. Uski baat check karo.
answer: No: 100° + 100° = 200°, already more than 180°, so no third angle can fit

subject: maths
prompt_en: Neha measured a big triangle on the playground: 70°, 60°, 50°. She says, 'Big triangles have a bigger sum, so maybe I missed something.' What is right?
prompt_hi: Neha ne maidan par bade triangle ke angle naape: 70°, 60°, 50°. Woh kehti hai, 'Bade triangle ka sum bada hota hai, shayad kuch chhoot gaya.' Sahi kya hai?
answer: Her measurement is right: 70° + 60° + 50° = 180°; size does not change the angle sum

subject: maths
prompt_en: In an isosceles triangle the top angle is 40° and the two base angles are equal. Find them.
prompt_hi: Ek isosceles triangle ka upar wala angle 40° hai aur neeche ke do angle barabar hain. Unhe nikaalo.
answer: 70° each

subject: maths
prompt_en: The roof frame of a hill house is a triangle. Each roof slope makes 35° with the ceiling beam. What is the angle at the top (the ridge)?
prompt_hi: Pahaadi ghar ki chhat ka frame triangle hai. Har dhalaan ceiling beam se 35° banati hai. Upar (ridge) ka angle kitna hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Describe how folding a paper triangle shows that its angles add to 180°.
prompt_hi: Batao ki kaagaz ke triangle ko modkar kaise dikhta hai ki uske angles ka jod 180° hai.
answer: Fold the top corner down to the foot of the altitude, then fold the two base corners in to the same point: the three angles fill a straight line, 180°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend why a triangle can never have two right angles.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki triangle mein kabhi do right angle kyun nahi ho sakte.
answer: Two right angles already make 180°, leaving 0° for the third; the two sides would be parallel and never meet

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: what is a scalene triangle?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: scalene triangle kya hota hai?
answer: A triangle with all three sides of different lengths (so all angles are different too)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Find 3 × 2/5.
prompt_hi: 3 × 2/5 nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_hi: 1/2 × 3/4 nikaalo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: Find 2/3 × 9/10 and simplify.
prompt_hi: 2/3 × 9/10 nikaalo aur simplify karo.
answer: 3/5 (18/30 simplified)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict before multiplying: will 18 × 2/3 be more or less than 18? Then calculate.
prompt_hi: Guna karne se pehle andaaza lagao: 18 × 2/3, 18 se zyada hoga ya kam? Phir nikaalo.
answer: Less: 2/3 is less than 1; 18 × 2/3 = 12

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare 2/5 + 3/5 and 2/5 × 3/5. Why is one equal to 1 and the other only 6/25?
prompt_hi: 2/5 + 3/5 aur 2/5 × 3/5 ko compare karo. Ek 1 ke barabar kyun hai aur doosra sirf 6/25?
answer: Adding fifths gives 5 fifths = 1; multiplying takes 2/5 of 3/5, a part of a part, which is 6 of 25 equal pieces

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why is 1/2 × 3/4 smaller than 3/4?
prompt_hi: 1/2 × 3/4, 3/4 se chhota kyun hai?
answer: It means half of 3/4, and half of anything is less than all of it

subject: maths
prompt_en: Kiran wrote 4 × 3/7 = 12/28. Check his work.
prompt_hi: Kiran ne likha 4 × 3/7 = 12/28. Uska kaam check karo.
answer: Wrong: only the number of pieces is multiplied, so 4 × 3/7 = 12/7; his 12/28 equals 3/7, which is not 4 times bigger

subject: maths
prompt_en: Divya wrote 3/4 × 1/4 = 3/4 'because the denominators are the same, so keep them'. Check her.
prompt_hi: Divya ne likha 3/4 × 1/4 = 3/4 'kyunki denominator same hain, wahi rakho'. Use check karo.
answer: Wrong: keeping the denominator is the addition habit; multiply the denominators too, so 3/4 × 1/4 = 3/16

subject: maths
prompt_en: A recipe needs 3/4 cup of sugar. You make half the recipe. How much sugar do you need?
prompt_hi: Ek recipe mein 3/4 cup cheeni chahiye. Tum aadhi recipe banate ho. Kitni cheeni chahiye?
answer: 3/8 cup

subject: maths
prompt_en: A farmer uses 2/3 of his field for wheat, and 3/4 of the wheat area is watered by the canal. What fraction of the whole field is canal-watered wheat?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan apne khet ka 2/3 gehun ke liye use karta hai, aur gehun wale hisse ka 3/4 nahar se seencha jaata hai. Poore khet ka kitna hissa nahar wala gehun hai?
